speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you noticed this skin condition on the left dorsal hand, and has it been spreading?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background. Does the lesion on your hand itch, burn, or bleed, and have you noticed any recent changes in its color or size?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. Given the description of a rough, sandpaper-like plaque on the sun-exposed dorsal hand of a 65-year-old with a history of sunbathing, this is consistent with a premalignant lesion caused by chronic UV exposure. While it is not cancerous, it requires removal or destruction to prevent progression to squamous cell carcinoma. I will proceed with cryotherapy for this lesion.
